findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE uses SUM aggregate, corrupting scores on duplicates
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the merges use `zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads, so a re-processed or duplicate payload present in both sets will have its score (end_timestamp_precise) summed/doubled instead of preserved. This corrupts time ordering, breaks zpopmin eviction (oldest-first) and zscan ordering. Use AGGREGATE MIN (or MAX) or ZADD NX semantics.

findings.title: Direct end_timestamp_precise access can crash consumer
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch does `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` with no fallback. Any message missing that field (old producer, schema evolution, bad payload) raises KeyError inside RunTask/BatchStep, failing the whole batch and blocking offset commit. The score is only needed for ZADD ordering and should use .get with a sane default like timestamp/now.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing allows crafted cursor to break queryset
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly allows `cursor.offset < 0` and slices as `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, so a user-supplied cursor string (value:offset:is_prev) with a negative offset triggers a 500. The comments claiming Django handles it automatically and that it is safe are wrong. Same issue in BasePaginator change at line 182 where is_prev preserves negative offset.

findings.title: Unvalidated pagination switch exposes untested paginator
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the new `optimized_pagination=true` flag is read raw from request.GET bypassing the serializer, and enabled for anyone with `has_global_access` (not just superuser/admin). This routes audit-log reads through OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True, an untested path with different boundary handling, widening attack surface on a sensitive audit endpoint.

findings.title: Removal of max_segment_spans guard leaves no fallback if eviction fails
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py _load_segment_data the check for `len(payloads[key]) > max_segment_spans` and `segment_span_count_exceeded` was deleted, leaving only byte-size guard. The Lua cap is hardcoded to 1000 while SpansBuffer defaults to max_segment_spans=1001, so the config is now dead. If the Lua script is old/cached, eviction is bypassed, or ZSET scores collide, oversized segments are now fully loaded into memory and produced instead of skipped.

findings.title: Redirect depth cut from 10000 to 1000 can split deep segments
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the redirect-chain loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segments with chain depth >1000 will stop resolving early and write to the wrong set_key, producing split or duplicated segments that never join. This is a correctness regression disguised as optimization.
